Done. Session summary:

## The lane is finished and PR #211 is ready

**The red was not mine, and I proved it rather than argued it.** Attempt 1 inferred this from the index blob matching master's — indirect, and weaker than it needed to be, because `nv2a_index.py check` *does* read `hw/xbox/**`, exactly where this lane's only change lives. So I ran the gate on a pristine `origin/master` worktree against upstream's real tip:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `lane/cloud190` | `1 suite(s) changed content …: Texture render target`, exit 1 |
| pristine `origin/master` (`3fe18366cd`), none of my branch present | **byte-identical message, exit 1** |

The drift is pinned, not guessed: upstream tests tip `c6755886df` was committed **2026-09-21T16:54Z** — one hour after the last green run (15:53Z), and every run from 21:24Z is red. The check clones upstream's tip at run time.

**The resolver has a number: PR #214 `lane/indexpin`** — open, ready, its own `check` *passes*. It pins the check to the index's own `provenance.tests_commit`, which is precisely what attempt 1's notes asked for. When it folds, merging master turns #211 green with no content change here. I marked that request ANSWERED in place rather than appending, so the old section no longer reads as outstanding.

**I did not regenerate the index.** It isn't this lane's file, and the only tests tree this host can reach is `6743b6ab16` — already the commit the committed index was built from. Rebuilding here re-commits the identical answer while looking like a fix.

## Two findings worth your attention

1. **`fold.sh`'s own remedy is unreachable from the state that needs it.** It rebuilds a stale index at line 750, but gates on `ci_green` at line 686 — which the stale index is what trips. `stale_red` doesn't rescue it either: this PR's runs started 34 min *after* master's tip was committed, so the red doesn't read as stale. #214 makes it moot, but the gate-ordering will outlive this drift.

2. **`preflight.sh` fails on the *coverage* gate, not the tracker gate**, so `--allow-tracker` doesn't clear it — it only reveals a second row (#207 says `open`, GitHub says CLOSED; #213 has neither a lane nor a blocker). Both reproduce under master's own `check_coverage.py`, and neither can be mine in principle: the gate reads `territory.toml` and `nv2a_issues.toml` from `origin/board`, never from my branch.

**Done-when:** pushed `3914c81000`; `Files:` matches the 7-path diffstat; NOTES.md written with attempt-1's header corrected in place; `Prediction: none` (no golden can see a PMC register read); both `build` jobs SUCCESS; #190 already carries the note confirming #188's `NV_PMC_ENABLE` was left alone; `[lane.cloud190] waiting:` comment posted; **PR marked ready**. `fold-ready` is the auditor's/board's label, not a lane's, and the board acts on ready PRs — that's the handoff.

I deliberately did not poll CI; the index check is red for the documented reason and will stay so until #214 folds.

Separately, the memory-index hook fired: I compacted `MEMORY.md` from 20.9KB to 14.5KB by tightening hooks only — all 101 entries kept, no broken links, and I filled a pre-existing gap (`dispatch-needs-worktree-isolation.md` had never been indexed).
